lines: A live number is gone in a second. Telo Ride now keeps the ride's totals: distance, output and energy.
Each running second adds the speed over thirty-six hundred to distance. An hour at thirty is thirty kilometres.
A paused ride has no running seconds, so its distance and output hold, however long the pause.
Each running second also adds its power over a thousand to the ride's output, in kilojoules.
Energy follows. Two hundred and eight watts for seven hundred and sixty seconds is a hundred and fifty-seven kilocalories.
An unknown value shows as a dash, never a stale number, and distance always shows two decimals.
Three kinds of readouts share these helpers: the class ride's tiles, the race power panel and the custom ride's dashboard.
On the simulated bike, a minute of frames turns into distance, output and energy, end to end.
Still to come: the ride clock ticks the totals in slice 5.1, and Class Ride first shows them in 5.2.
Home doesn't change yet, at any width. The totals wait in the engine for the ride screens.
What the tests prove: twenty new unit tests, one per row of the requirements, and every spec still green.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
